stem: A febrile young infant has noisy breathing; which sound-pattern pairing is correctly matched?
explanation: Inspiratory stridor indicates upper airway obstruction.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Emergency Medicine/Surgery - Recognising and Managing the Sick Child

optionExplanations.A: Correct because inspiratory stridor is produced by upper airway obstruction.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because inspiratory stridor is a sign of upper, not lower, airway obstruction.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because expiratory wheeze is more consistent with lower airway narrowing, not subglottic obstruction.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because biphasic stridor suggests fixed upper airway obstruction, not airspace disease.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because grunting reflects lower airway or alveolar disease with expiratory effort, not an isolated secretion problem.
